thread:
devbot: INCIDENT: P0 - high request latency and 502s on /v1/generate - paging @alice_ops @ben_infra @carla_sre :rotating_light:

alice_ops: paging in. I’m on it. seeing sustained 95th pct latency spikes on hosted cluster A (us-west1). customers reporting timeouts.

ben_infra: on my way. can you drop the quick metrics? queue depth, GPU utilization?

alice_ops: pulling dashboards. quick snapshot: 
- request queue depth to gpu-pool-7: 342 (baseline ~40)
- GPU utilization: 97% on pool-7 nodes, others at 20-30%
- Pod restart noise: increased warmup latencies after scale events

carla_sre: any recent deploys?

alice_ops: no code deploys in last 2 hours. autoscaler events kicked in at 14:02 UTC. lots of HPA up events but pods stayed Pending for ~40s each.

ben_infra: that Pending sounds like warmup/image pull or GPUs not available. checking k8s events...

ben_infra: k8s events snippet: ```
14:02:11 HPA scaled up from 6 to 12 replicas
14:02:12 Pod "infer-xx" failed scheduling: 0/12 nodes are available: insufficient nvidia.com/gpu.
14:02:54 Pod "infer-yy" scheduled on node-46
14:03:35 Pod "infer-yy" container start failed: init-warmup-timeout
```

alice_ops: so HPA tried to scale but GPU pool was saturated. nodes that did schedule then hit warmup timeout (init container stuck).

sam_support: customers seeing 502/504. surfacing top affected customers: org-172, org-9 (chat apps). they see timeouts around 14:04-14:08 UTC.

carla_sre: hypothesis A: sudden traffic spike + slow node acquisition -> queue pileup -> long tail latency -> upstream 502s. Hypothesis B: image-pull or init-warmup regression causing pods to take too long and HPA unable to add ready capacity.

ben_infra: checking cloud provider logs for GPU allocation. There was an across-cluster maintenance window earlier but supposedly drained nodes were returned at 13:58. Might be node fragmentation: GPUs exist but not in desired sizes.

alice_ops: copying relevant logs for timeline: ```
13:55:00 traffic uptick begins (x2 baseline)
14:01:45 autoscaler triggers HPA to target 12
14:02:11 cluster autoscaler requests 6 additional nodes with gpu type A
14:02:30 cloud returns 6 nodes but they come as tainted for maintenance for ~1min
14:02:55 pods enter Pending due to insufficient free gpus
14:03:15 first pods scheduled but init-warmup (warmup container) hangs - logs show failed nvlib init
14:03:40 controller marks some pods Failed (init timeout)
14:04:00 queue depth peaks, requests start timing out, upstream returns 502s
14:07:00 mitigation: manual borrow from dedicated pool started
14:08:30 partial recovery as borrowed nodes accept pods
14:12:00 traffic returns to baseline
```

carla_sre: good concise timeline. action items in-thread: 1) short-term mitigation - drain low-priority jobs to free GPUs, 2) investigate init-warmup failure cause, 3) improve HPA to consider GPU provisioning latency, 4) postmortem owners.

alice_ops: executed mitigation 1 at 14:07:05 - cordoned / low-prio batch queue and drained 4 jobs. latencies improved after 14:09. customers still saw some errors until 14:12.

ben_infra: debug of init-warmup logs: ```
[init-warmup] ERROR: cuInit failed: CUDA driver version mismatch
[init-warmup] Retrying...
[init-warmup] ERROR: timed out after 30s
```

ben_infra: looks like driver mismatch on some returned nodes (maintenance nodes). cloud had rotated drivers during maintenance. pods that landed there failed warmup.

sam_support: customers + CS notes: org-172 reported 30-45s timeouts causing UX retries. escalated to AE for affected accounts.

carla_sre: Root cause candidate: race between autoscaler provisioning (new nodes) and node maintenance returning with incompatible GPU drivers. This caused scheduling to be delayed and several init-warmup failures, creating a capacity shortfall and queue buildup.

alice_ops: temporary workaround: add a pre-check in node-acceptance that validates GPU driver compatibility before marking as schedulable. Also add a retry backoff to warmup init to allow second chance if driver updated within window.

ben_infra: longer-term: 1) make HPA consider cluster-provision latency (scale buffer), 2) warmup container logs to S3 and alert on cuInit errors, 3) health-check taint clearing process to validate drivers.

carla_sre: we should quantify impact: estimated failed requests ~ 18k, affected customers ~ 12 orgs, incident duration ~ 14:02 - 14:12 (10m). add SLA blameless note.

alice_ops: taking on incident writeup. assigning owners: ben_infra -> infra RCA (driver rotation + cloud API), carla_sre -> timeline & mitigations, alice_ops -> mitigation automation + runbook. sam_support -> customer comms + impact tally.

ben_infra: quick follow up: I'll open cloud support ticket about driver rotation and request driver pin on returned nodes.

carla_sre: we'll also add an in-thread hypothesis table to track evidence: 
- Hypothesis A (traffic spike): evidence = traffic x2, but autoscaler triggered -> partial
- Hypothesis B (node driver mismatch): evidence = cuInit errors in warmup logs, nodes returned after maintenance; high
- Hypothesis C (scheduler fragmentation): evidence = Pending due to insufficient gpu on some nodes; medium

alice_ops: marking incident as mitigated at 14:12. leaving thread for postmortem workstream.

devbot: Note: Incident P0 closed (mitigated). Please file incident postmortem using /postmortem and tag #eng-oncall.

sam_support: I’ll draft customer-facing summary and share with CS.

carla_sre: follow-up tasks created in backlog. Will schedule RCA sync tomorrow 10:00 UTC.

alice_ops: thanks everyone. actions: blameless review, metrics augment, HPA buffer. :thumbsup:
